questions.q: Propanoic acid is warmed with Br₂ and a small amount of red phosphorus, followed by water. The product is:
questions.explain: The halogen enters the α-carbon through the enol of the acyl bromide; because the α-carbon is planar in the enol, the new stereocentre forms as a racemic mixture.

questions.q: Which carboxylic acid does NOT undergo the Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction?
questions.explain: HVZ needs at least one α-hydrogen to form the enol. (CH₃)₃C–COOH has a quaternary α-carbon, like benzoic acid and formic acid, which also fail.

questions.q: Propanoic acid is treated with Cl₂ in the presence of PBr₃, then water. The main product is:
questions.explain: The phosphorus halide only makes the acyl halide; the α-halogen comes from the free halogen that attacks the enol. So Cl₂/PBr₃ gives the α-chloro acid and Br₂/PCl₃ the α-bromo acid.

questions.q: Acetic acid is converted into glycine. The correct reagent sequence is:
questions.explain: HVZ gives bromoacetic acid, and the reactive α-bromine is then replaced by NH₂ with excess ammonia to give H₂N–CH₂–COOH. PCl₅ alone gives only the acyl chloride, with no α-substitution.
